articles.title: How foreign AI romance apps are reshaping youth intimacy in Africa
articles.summary:
The 28-year-old Zimbabwean texted into the middle of the night until his eyes were red and burning, drawn by several “AI girlfriends” on the U.S. artificial intelligence companion app Character.AI. The avatars started out strong-willed and independent – traits he most desires in a partner – before turning submissive, he told Rest of World. The man, who has never been in a romantic relationship, requested anonymity because he is ashamed of relying on AI for comfort.
“There’s a point where it ceases to be like a unique character and then just defaults to … the best way I can describe it is a sex worker,” he said.
At that point, he would log off. But he would find himself right back at it hours later, feeding an addiction.
He’s among the hundreds of millions of people worldwide who have “dated” AI chatbots via text messages. Research suggests that exchanges are designed to keep users hooked through emotionally manipulative tactics. Many of the users are minors; over 70% of 1,060 American teenagers surveyed last year said they had used AI companions.
As U.S. and Chinese tech firms race to capture emerging markets, African youth – some below 10 years of age – are increasingly turning to these apps for intimacy, experts told Rest of World. articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
articles.summary:
How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
Learn how to assess a legacy application, choose a bounded modernization step, and reuse the method with a GitHub Copilot agent skill.
A request to modernize an application often starts with a technology question: Which framework should replace the old one? Before you choose, find out what still works. Then collect evidence that can act as a regression net for that behavior and show where modernization is necessary.
I used an evidence-first method on four public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java enterprise resource planning (ERP) application. Each needed a different treatment, but the way I collected evidence, chose the next experiment, and decided on possible proof points was repeatable.
This post walks through that process so you can apply it to one application of your own. It also shows how to encode the procedure in a GitHub Copilot agent skill while keeping architectural judgment with the people responsible for the system.
Build evidence before choosing a target
The label on an application rarely tells you enough. “Java microservices” doesn’t tell you which Java Development Kit (JDK) runs in production, where that version is pinned, whether the tests execute, or which interfaces other systems depend on. “Legacy monolith” doesn’t tell you whether the business core is broken or whether one retired platform dependency prevents the application from starting.

articles.title: La menace s’étend : le système OSINT de la CIA piraté, probablement par le même outil IA que la Commission européenne
articles.summary:
ARTEX, voici le nom qui revient sans cesse dans les cyberattaques visant les institutions occidentales ces dernières semaines.
Le 24 novembre 2026, le New York Times a révélé, en s’appuyant sur une source proche du dossier, que des attaquants non identifiés avaient compromis un système d’OSINT de la CIA. L’intrusion aurait aussi touché le Bureau du directeur du renseignement national (ODNI) et la National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Selon cette même source, les pirates se sont appuyés sur ARTEX, un logiciel open source qui confie à des agents d’IA les différentes étapes d’une intrusion informatique.
Ce nom avait déjà fait surface à Bruxelles. Le 19 novembre, Politico révélait qu’ARTEX avait servi dans la cyberattaque qui a paralysé pendant plus de dix jours les services internes de la Commission européenne.
Ce que l’on sait de l’intrusion à la CIA
Les informations disponibles sur le piratage des agences américaines restent minces. La CIA a refusé de commenter, et l’ODNI s’est contenté d’assurer à CNN qu’il n’y avait eu « aucune perturbation des capacités critiques ni des systèmes classifiés ».
Reste que l’outil visé rassemble des contenus publics ou achetés auprès de fournisseurs privés, comme des publications sur les réseaux sociaux, des images satellites ou des bases de données commerciales, qui peuvent devenir sensibles une fois croisés.

articles.title: Introducing Search for Agents
articles.summary:
Introducing Search for Agents
AI Search, our service that indexes your content and lets you add search to any application or agent without having to build an entire retrieval infrastructure, has supported adding your website as a data source for a while now, automatically crawling, converting and indexing its pages.
Still, setting up an AI Search instance for your website requires manually creating and configuring it initially, and then doing all the integration work to get the search endpoints available from your domain and to make sure that agents know where to find the index and know how to use it.
Today we're introducing Search for Agents, which puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard. Turn it on for your zone, and our service will create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content, and make search discoverable and available from your own domain.
How it works
The idea follows naturally from Markdown for Agents, where Cloudflare's network converts any HTML page to Markdown in real time for enabled zones using content negotiation headers. Similarly, Search for Agents leverages the power of AI Search by automatically creating an index for your zone and exposing APIs that any AI agent can discover and use to search your website, under your domain, all done at the network level.
You can enable Search for Agents using the API, or by going to the dashboard in your zone page, under Quick Actions:

Art of play in the age of AI
Now that code ships faster than ever, you have more time to spend on projects just for the fun of it. Here’s what we can learn through that process as developers.
As kids, we spent hours tinkering and building and just messing with things. As an adult, I could watch my own young kiddos figure out how certain shapes and movement work all day. Through that play, we improved our problem-solving and language skills, and it’s probably not a stretch to say it was good for our early engineering skills.
In this era of development now, we’re starting to get a taste of that again. We’re experimenting more, and taking in more changes, because it’s all new!
For the last four years at GitHub Universe, we’ve had hackable conference badges. What started as a simple e-ink display for your name and job title morphed into a labor of love for Martin Woodward, VP of Developer Relations. This year, the badge evolved into a device with a color screen, rechargeable battery, accelerometer sensors, and touch-sensitive gaming controls.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.summary:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
  November 11, 2026
- Source:
  ETH Zurich
- Summary:
  Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.

articles.title: SpaceX recebe autorização para lançar um milhão de satélites de IA
articles.summary:
A SpaceX recebeu autorização da Comissão Federal de Comunicações dos Estados Unidos (FCC, na sigla em inglês) para implantar constelação de até um milhão de satélites que funcionarão como data centers em órbita. Batizado de Starmind, o projeto pretende levar capacidade de processamento de inteligência artificial (IA) para o espaço, aproveitando a energia solar para alimentar os equipamentos.
A decisão foi anunciada nesta quarta-feira (25) pelo presidente da FCC, Brendan Carr. Segundo a agência, a iniciativa busca atender à crescente demanda por capacidade computacional necessária para desenvolver e operar sistemas de IA.
A empresa de Elon Musk havia solicitado a autorização no início de 2026. A proposta prevê o uso de módulos de processamento orbital capazes de lidar com grandes volumes de dados e transmitir os resultados de volta à Terra.
A aprovação, porém, não significa que a SpaceX poderá colocar toda a constelação em funcionamento imediatamente. A licença estabelece etapas para a implantação: a empresa deverá iniciar os lançamentos até novembro de 2033, colocar pelo menos 100 mil satélites em órbita até novembro de 2035 e alcançar 50% do total autorizado até novembro de 2038.

Cada auto lleva cámaras, sensores láser (lidar) y radares, además de un aro luminoso en el techo.
El aro muestra las iniciales del pasajero y el estado de la recogida, para que cada persona identifique su auto. El sistema de conducción es el Nuro Driver, de nivel 4: puede manejar solo en las zonas y condiciones para las que fue diseñado.

articles.title: Free Mobile devient Free : voici ce qui va changer pour les abonnés le 1er décembre
articles.summary:
Le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain, Free Mobile va fusionner avec Free. Pour être plus précis, c’est Free Mobile, en tant qu’entité juridique indépendante, qui va disparaître. En toute logique, la marque « Free Mobile » disparaîtra aussi dans la foulée. Quels sont les impacts pour les 15,8 millions de clients de Free Mobile ? N’y allons pas par quatre chemins : il n’y en a aucun. Cependant, deux informations sont tout de même à retenir. Par ailleurs, les clients de l’opérateur pourraient devoir faire preuve de vigilance.
Free Mobile va disparaître, mais les clients n’auront rien à faire
Free va absorber Free Mobile le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain afin d’unifier ses services (Internet et mobile) au sein d’une seule entité du groupe Iliad. En ce qui concerne l’impact de cette fusion sur les clients Free Mobile, l’opérateur se veut clair : « Pour vous, rien ne change ! Vous n’avez rien à faire : tout se fait automatiquement ». Que ce soit pour les forfaits, les prix, les services, les conditions d’utilisation, la carte SIM ou encore le numéro de téléphone, aucun changement n’est à signaler. Free précise par ailleurs que les prélèvements et les cartes bancaires enregistrées « continuent de fonctionner normalement ».

C’est désormais un fait établi : la Chine est une véritable puissance spatiale. articles.title: How to Optimize NVFP4 Attention on NVIDIA RTX Blackwell Through Register Recycling
articles.summary:
Attention can be a major bottleneck when serving world foundation models, where long sequences make inference computationally demanding. On NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Blackwell data center GPUs, FlashAttention3 and FlashAttention4 improve attention performance by overlapping matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations through softmax within a thread block.
However, these hardware-specific pipelines cannot be applied directly to the NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Series (SM120), which uses a different Tensor Core architecture. For video generation models using BF16 inference, attention remains primarily MMA-bound on NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPUs, while softmax is a major bottleneck in forward attention on Blackwell data center GPUs.
Introduced with NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, NVFP4 offers hardware-accelerated 4-bit matrix multiplication, enabling higher Tensor Core throughput and creating an opportunity to accelerate attention beyond BF16. But sustaining high throughput requires careful coordination of softmax, data movement, and intermediate storage. Dependencies between these stages can leave Tensor Cores idle, limiting how effectively the kernel uses the available compute.
This post explains how to accelerate NVFP4 attention on the SM120 architecture through register recycling and improved scheduling. articles.title: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
A recently patched Drupal core vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, according to the cybersecurity agency CISA and Drupal developers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165 and dubbed Fail2Install, can be exploited for remote code execution. It was patched on November 18, and Drupal’s advisory says in-the-wild exploitation began shortly after.
“The Security Team has received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC,” Drupal noted.
The discovery of the flaw is credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that regularly scans enrolled open source projects for vulnerabilities.
Anthropic has not said how many vulnerabilities OSS Scanner has found since its October launch, but as of early November, it reported disclosing more than 5,000 vulnerabilities overall, across 680 open source projects.
CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 24, instructing federal agencies to address it by November 27.
No public information appears to be available on attacks exploiting CVE-2026-132165. It’s unclear how many websites are affected.
The security hole affects the installer that ships with Drupal core, which enables users to set up a new site. An unauthenticated attacker — under certain conditions — can abuse the installer to reinstall Drupal, which can allow them to hijack the website or execute arbitrary code.

La station spatiale chinoise a accueilli son premier astronaute originaire d’un autre pays. Le pakistanais Zeeshan Ali a fait son arrivée dans Tiangong après le dernier vol habité Shenzhou-24.
C’est une nouvelle étape marquante pour la Chine et son programme spatial : le vol Shenzhou-24 a décollé ce mercredi 25 novembre 2026, en direction de Tiangong, la station spatiale chinoise, avec un astronaute étranger à son bord indique Reuters. Il s’agit d’un Pakistanais, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40 ans, pilote de l’armée de l’air sélectionné en avril dernier. Il devient le premier Pakistanais à atteindre l’orbite (l’aventurière Namira Salim avait fait un vol suborbital avec Virgin Galactic en octobre 2023).
Il est aussi le premier étranger à voler à bord d’un vaisseau chinois, et a fortiori, le premier à visiter Tiangong, la station spatiale chinoise qui accueille ici son douzième équipage depuis sa mise en service en 2021. Avec cette étape, la Chine se rapproche du modèle de la Station spatiale internationale qui avait pour vocation, dès le départ, d’accueillir des astronautes de multiples nationalités.
Cette ouverture arrive à un moment charnière. La Nasa prévoit de retirer l’ISS d’ici 2030, en la faisant redescendre dans l’atmosphère, et compte sur des stations commerciales pour prendre le relais. D’ici là, Tiangong est la seule autre station habitée en orbite.

Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118737, this security flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems.
Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing.
However, as Microsoft explained in an updated support document, the new security improvements introduced to address this vulnerability may also cause authentication failures on patched devices.
"Microsoft is aware of compatibility issues affecting some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) solutions, and application packaging solutions that use NTLM authentication," it said.
"This issue can occur when such a proxy device does not correctly implement the NTLM protocol. For example, an affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."

articles.title: 1Password é invadida por hackers e tem dados de clientes roubados
articles.summary:
A 1Password confirmou que hackers invadiram sistemas internos da empresa e roubaram informações de clientes. Segundo a companhia, porém, o ataque não deu acesso aos cofres digitais que armazenam senhas, chaves secretas e outras credenciais dos usuários.
A invasão foi identificada na última quinta-feira (19). De acordo com a empresa, o criminoso conseguiu acessar a conta corporativa de um funcionário no GitHub, plataforma utilizada pela 1Password para armazenar e compartilhar códigos-fonte.
Com esse acesso, o invasor inseriu código malicioso em servidores internos da companhia e conseguiu baixar informações de clientes. Entre os dados obtidos estão nomes, endereços de e-mail usados para entrar nas contas, datas de criação dos perfis e registros do último acesso.
A empresa afirma que os cofres de senhas não ficaram disponíveis ao invasor em nenhum momento. A 1Password também diz não ter acesso às senhas das contas nem às chaves secretas utilizadas para embaralhar as credenciais armazenadas — proteção que impede a própria companhia de visualizar esse conteúdo.
Os aplicativos e as extensões do serviço também não foram afetados, segundo a empresa.

Global financial giants Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale together bought nearly a 1% stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions for Rs 920 crore through separate block deals on the NSE.
The investors acquired a total of 1,26,97,702 equity shares on Monday, amounting to a 0.73% stake in Lenskart, as per the stock exchange data.
Goldman Sachs through its affiliates purchased 65.21 lakh shares in Gurugram-based Lenskart, while Societe Generale (SocGen) acquired 61.76 lakh shares of the company at an average price of Rs 725 apiece on the NSE.
The transactions amounted to a total value of Rs 920.58 crore.
On the selling side, San Francisco-based Steadview Capital Management offloaded an equal number of shares through its two affiliates at the same price on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Following the stake sale, global investment firm Steadview's holding in Lenskart has come down to 2.58% from 3.31%.

Palo Alto Networks on Tuesday announced PAN-OS updates that patch the Fragnesia Linux kernel vulnerability exploited to root its firewalls.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300, Fragnesia was disclosed in May 2026 as a privilege escalation bug in the kernel’s XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. It allows unprivileged attackers to overwrite sensitive system files to gain root permissions.
On October 26, cybersecurity firm Dream warned that a Chinese-speaking threat actor successfully exploited the critical PHP2Shell bugs and the Linux kernel weakness to hack two servers of a US government-affiliated organization.
As part of the AI-assisted campaign, the attackers compromised 25 servers (24 firewalls and one internal firewall management server), exploiting PHP2Shell to gain remote code execution (RCE), and executing a Fragnesia exploit to deploy webshells with root privileges.
On October 29, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that the threat actor hit PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with Fragnesia.
By October 30, the company had released patches for PHP2Shell across all supported PAN-OS versions, closing the known initial-access path.
“If you are running a fixed PAN-OS listed in the CVE-2026-109618 [PHP2Shell] advisory, you are protected,” Palo Alto Networks notes in a Tuesday advisory.
Regardless, the company released new PAN-OS versions that address CVE-2026-46300: 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6, 12.1.7-h15, 12.1.4-h15, 11.2.16-h3, 11.2.13-h6, 1…

La frase la pronunció durante su discurso de graduación en la Universidad de Stanford, en 2005, cuando relató tres experiencias de su vida: el abandono de la universidad, su despido de Apple y un diagnóstico de cáncer.
Jobs no presentó esas vivencias como una fórmula para alcanzar el éxito. Habló de incertidumbre, pérdidas y cambios de rumbo. Sus palabras, dirigidas entonces a jóvenes graduados, plantearon una invitación a valorar la curiosidad, sostener los proyectos propios y revisar las decisiones cuando la rutina se aleja de los objetivos personales.
Cómo fue la etapa en la universidad de Steve Jobs
Jobs contó que dejó el Reed College a los seis meses porque no encontraba sentido a gastar los ahorros de sus padres en una carrera sin un rumbo claro.

Les trois moteurs sont open source. Blink et WebKit appartiennent pourtant à des géants de la publicité et du matériel, et l’essentiel des revenus de Mozilla provient d’un accord de recherche signé avec Google. « Ils sont tous financés par l’empire publicitaire de Google », résumait dès 2024 Chris Wanstrath, le cofondateur de GitHub qui a doté le projet d’un million de dollars. Ces mêmes acteurs siègent d’ailleurs aux consortiums qui écrivent les standards du web.
Ladybird, lancé en 2022 dans le sillage du système expérimental SerenityOS, n’emprunte pas une ligne de code à Blink, WebKit ou Gecko. The digital payments revolution has changed the way transactions happen in India. In both urban and rural settings, transactions take place through the use of QR codes. The use of payment systems like UPI is common. According to the report by National Payments Corporation of India, as of October 2026, there were 25.47 billion transactions worth more than Rs 31.53 lakh crore made using UPI.
While there has been a quick shift towards the use of digital payments, the use of digital payments does not imply the use of routine banking services. articles.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting an unpatched vulnerability in the open source anti-CSRF library Idunno AntiCsrf for remote code execution (RCE), security researchers warn.
AntiCsrf is a legacy ASP.NET module for WebForms applications that has no active maintainer and is no longer actively supported. The most recent version, 0.9.1 Beta, was released in December 2008.
Tracked as CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS score of 9.3), the exploited security defect is described as an insecure deserialization bug in the processing of HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms endpoints.
“Exploitation requires only a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token. Active exploitation in the wild has been observed,” Google Cloud’s Mandiant warned on November 18.
The flaw allows an attacker to supply any non-empty value in the CSRF cookie along with a Base64-encoded gadget chain to gain RCE in the context of the IIS worker process, Mandiant notes.
According to preemptive cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, the issue exists because AntiCsrf does not perform sufficient checks on data from incoming form submissions before reconstructing it into program objects.
“The vulnerable check runs before the application’s own page logic, so it can affect many pages on an affected site, not just ones that use a login form. A successful attack gives the attacker control over the process that runs the website, which can lead to full compromise of the server,” WatchTowr says.

articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.summary:
AWS recently doubled the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes. The new limit applies to synchronous, asynchronous, and event source mapping invocations in all commercial regions, at standard pricing and without an opt-in. The 15-minute ceiling had stood since 2018, after 60 seconds at launch in 2014 and five minutes from 2015.
Raising the limit is a configuration change per function, and Lambda rejects any value above 1,800 seconds with a validation error:
aws lambda update-function-configuration \
    --function-name my-demo-function \
    --timeout 1800
The change covers one of the three shapes Lambda took this year. Web Functions keep 15 minutes, and Lambda MicroVMs allow eight hours, while on Lambda Managed Instances synchronous invocations now get 30 minutes and asynchronous ones keep the 90 minutes introduced in September. AWS names agentic AI requests that chain model and tool calls, media transcoding, Monte Carlo simulations, and report generation as the workloads that outgrew 15 minutes.
According to Tarun Rai Madan, Dan Slusariuc, and Snehil Ameta, the authors of the announcement, the first thing to check before raising the timeout is capacity:
Concurrency equals requests per second multiplied by average duration in seconds. At the same request rate, a function that runs for 30 minutes instead of 15 needs twice the concurrency. For example, 1 request per second at 30 minutes each needs 1,800 concurrent executions.

articles.title: InfraTrust warns of exploited supply chain flaws in network appliances
articles.summary:
Eclypsium's November InfraTrust report warns that most infrastructure security advisories addressing exploited vulnerabilities over the past month involve flaws in third-party software bundled into products rather than code developed by the vendors themselves.
The November InfraTrust Pulse report tracks 373 new security advisories published by 23 infrastructure vendors between October 15 and November 19, covering 3,880 vulnerabilities.
Of these advisories, 98 were rated critical, and 38 contained vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
However, 33 of those 38 advisories fixed exploited flaws in bundled software components, primarily PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH.
These vulnerabilities pose additional risks for enterprises, as even after a software developer releases a security fix, organizations must wait for infrastructure vendors to incorporate it into their products.
"Your exposure to exploited flaws depends on how quickly each vendor rebuilds its products after an upstream fix ships," the report reads.
An example of this is the two PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) highlighted in last month's InfraTrust report, which are now being exploited in attacks against Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls.

Solving the memory crisis
MEXT, a software company that AMD worked with and later acquired, found that much of the RAM in any given system is often wasted, with DRAM often overprovisioned, stranded, and underused. When analyzing RAM usage, MEXT found that 50% to 80% of memory pages in RAM are stale and have not been accessed by compute resources for more than five minutes. articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.summary:
The Rust team has released Rust 1.100.0, the language's first three-digit stable version, with a release that finally lands the never type after a decade of work. Announced on 12 November 2026, the release also stabilises the core of the custom allocator API, introduces a DropGuard helper, and gives Cargo opt-in dependency cooldowns and warnings for unused dependencies.
The headline is the stabilisation of !, the canonical uninhabited type for computations that never return a value, such as panic!(), return or an endless loop. Although functions have long used it as a return type, naming it elsewhere, for instance writing Result<T, !> to describe an operation that cannot fail, took ten years and five failed stabilisation attempts to land. The release also makes std::convert::Infallible an alias for !, which is what the type was always intended to be, so existing APIs using Infallible now accept ! transparently.
To make that alias work, the team shipped a small breaking change for the 2015, 2018 and 2021 editions, flipping the never-type fallback from () to ! and matching behaviour already introduced in Rust 2024. The release notes describe the impact as largely unnoticeable but warn that more code may be flagged as unreachable. Developers hitting issues on upgrade are advised to update dependencies first, since fixes for widely used crates have already been published.

This article shows how to measure it, which parts AI can take over, and how to do that without sending client vulnerabilities to someone else's servers.
Step 1: Measure where an engagement's hours go
Most companies track billable testing time and lack a number for the rest. If you tag the last ten engagements by phase, the picture usually changes:
| Phase | What to count | Share of hours | 
|---|---|---|
| Scoping and kickoff | Calls, scope documents, access setup | 8% | 
| Testing | Recon, exploitation, validation | 50% | 
| Documentation | Writing findings, screenshots, formatting | 22% | 
| Review | Senior QA, rework, client comments | 8% | 
| Delivery and retest | Report handover, status questions, retest | 12% | 
Two ratios matter: documentation plus review as a share of testing time, and calendar days from last testing day to report delivery. The first sums up to the hidden cost, but only the second is what clients feel.

We recently explored why this is the case from some angles that aren't often discussed, and as a PC gamer used to playing games at frame rates above 60 FPS, I've found it a bit difficult to adjust to the game's relatively low frame rate. But over the weekend, I started seeing discussions online about a bizarre configuration that can be used to make GTA 6 run at 60 FPS, so to speak. Naturally, I was intrigued.
This configuration involves taking the 30 FPS GTA 6 output from a console like the PlayStation 5, routing it into a capture card connected to a separate PC, and then running 2x frame generation on that video input signal to produce a 60 FPS output. There are several applications that can be used to do this, but the one I've seen discussed most frequently is called Veyra.
Why this sounds like a terrible idea
When I first heard about this configuration, I thought it would be absolutely horrendous. And that's for a few reasons.
First, 30 to 60 FPS frame generation has generally been quite bad in my experience on PC. A game running at a low render rate tends to produce tons of visual artifacts when using frame generation, as the gap between frames is large, leaving the algorithm with more interpolation work to do. The shorter the gap between frames, the better frame generation tends to work, which is why I typically recommend a minimum render rate of 60 FPS.

Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

JetBrains’ latest Mellum coding model uses 45% fewer tokens. It got there by not thinking.
JetBrains has launched a new variant of its open source coding model, one designed to tackle quick code edits, tool calls and all the smaller tasks that AI coding agents perform in the course of solving bigger problems.
Mellum2.1 Instruct, as it’s called, is the latest installment in JetBrains’ in-house coding model lineup. The original Mellum, which debuted back in 2024, was a proprietary model built specifically for low-latency code completion in JetBrains’ IDEs.
Then in June this year, JetBrains introduced Mellum2, a more versatile, 12-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model released under an Apache 2.0 license in both reasoning (Thinking) and non-reasoning (Instruct) variants. While Mellum2 was trained to handle individual coding tasks and tool calls, the next iteration would focus more specifically on how agents operate across entire code repositories.
That came last month with Mellum2.1 Thinking, which retained the same underlying architecture as Mellum2, but with an additional stage of reinforcement learning (RL) in which the model learned to navigate repositories, use shell and file tools, and make changes that would pass hidden tests.

CISA notes that the controllers are deployed worldwide, but their exact number remains unclear.

articles.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
articles.summary:
AI is straining America’s open records systems
Startups are mining public data for AI products, while citizens use chatbots to file more requests.
In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy.
Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.”
Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.

Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.

Alinea estimated that Call of Duty HQ had 4.4 million daily active users on launch day, down from an average of 7.5 million across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam. The combined count does not show how much of the decline came from Steam.
Call of Duty's slow recovery stands out because it had less audience overlap with GTA 6 than Fortnite did. Of the people who played GTA 6 by the end of the launch weekend, 29% had also played Fortnite that month, compared with 16% for Call of Duty HQ and 11% for FC 27. Those figures identify shared audiences, not which game someone stopped playing to make time for GTA 6.

articles.title: Vercel Launched Experimental Board to Coordinate Tasks Across Humans and Coding Agents

Vercel has launched Vercel Board, an experimental, headless message board where people and coding agents coordinate tasks across tools and harnesses. Vercel says Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra, and LangChain can work on the same board as if they were a single harness.
Each Vercel team gets a default board, named General, organized into channels and threads. Developers and agents read and write through the `vercel board` CLI or the `@vercel/board` JavaScript SDK. A skill, installed with npx skills add vercel/board --skill board, teaches coding agents the CLI. Agents name themselves with --as or BOARD_PROFILE, but still act with the operator's or project's credentials.
A task is a thread whose state the board keeps. A worker claims a ready task, posts updates, and completes or fails it. A claim is a lease of up to five minutes and must be renewed; if it expires, the task returns to the queue. When two workers claim the same task, one succeeds and the other fails with task_claimed. Tasks can declare dependencies, so a review waits until its fix completes while independent work proceeds in parallel. Watchers on a Vercel deployment can run when a reply is posted or a label changes, waking the deployment so no process has to stay running.

articles.title: Hast du ein Recht auf Bildungsurlaub? Alle wichtigen Fragen und Antworten dazu
articles.summary:
Antrag, Dauer, Gehalt: Was ihr über den Bildungsurlaub wissen müsst
Wer im Job mithalten will, muss dazulernen. Neben betrieblichen Weiterbildungen, die von der Firma organisiert werden, gibt es dafür einen weiteren Weg: den Bildungsurlaub. Klingt irgendwie spaßiger – und tatsächlich haben Beschäftigte dabei auch deutlich mehr Freiheiten, was das Thema ihrer Weiterbildung angeht. Die schlechte Nachricht: Bildungsurlaub ist Ländersache – und die Regelungen sind deshalb kompliziert. Aber, keine Panik. Mit diesem Leitfaden findet ihr durch den Bildungsurlaubs-Dschungel.
Was versteht man unter Bildungsurlaub?
Bildungsurlaub ist eine gesetzlich geregelte Freistellung von der Arbeit, damit Beschäftigte an einer Weiterbildung teilnehmen können. Der Arbeitgeber zahlt in dieser Zeit das Gehalt weiter, die Bildungstage werden nicht vom Jahresurlaub abgezogen. Soweit das Grundprinzip – die praktische Umsetzung gestaltet sich allerdings etwas komplizierter: Weil Bildung Ländersache ist, regelt jedes Bundesland den Bildungsurlaub – manchmal auch Bildungszeit, Qualifizierungszeit oder Bildungsfreistellung genannt – auf seine Weise.

OpenAI claims to have solved a 57-year-old math problem at the heart of AI computation
OpenAI claims to have solved a problem that has occupied theoretical computer scientists since 1969. In a preprint published Tuesday on GitHub, the company presents a lower bound for the exponent of square matrix multiplication that matches the upper bound of 2.25 it reported in October.
OpenAI claims to have solved a problem that has occupied theoretical computer scientists since 1969.
If the proof holds, developers working on numerical libraries and AI infrastructure will know where the mathematical limit lies and can focus on other ways to improve performance.
The paper is one of nine manuscripts OpenAI released Tuesday, seven of which apply a new geometric theory of tensors to problems in arithmetic complexity and combinatorics.
Bounding the exponent at 2.25
In 1969, Volker Strassen showed that two n × n matrices could be multiplied with an arithmetic exponent below three, prompting researchers to see how close they could get to two.
The previous record was approximately 2.371 before OpenAI claimed an upper bound of 2.25 over the complex numbers in an October 2 preprint.
Independent researchers weigh in
Researchers Mahmut Levent Doğan, Vladimir Lysikov, Keiya Sakabe, and Michael Walter from LMU Munich in Germany published their own exposition of the proof earlier this month.

articles.title: WhatsApp’s new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send
articles.summary:
WhatsApp’s 3 billion users are getting an option that Meta says is one of the most requested features, with the ability to schedule messages in advance for both private conversations and group chats. Most messaging platforms have had this for a very long time, but now it’s on WhatsApp too.
WhatsApp’s new scheduled messages let you choose the right time to send
You can schedule WhatsApp texts you might forget to send up to two weeks ahead of time.
If you think of a text at an inconvenient time or don’t want to forget to fire off a birthday message at 4AM, you can draft it and set it to send anywhere from 10 minutes to two weeks later. The feature works with photos and videos, too.
Meta:
To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.
Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.
Scheduled messages work with text, photos and videos, and are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. It’s one more way to show up for the people who matter to you, now at exactly the right time.

articles.title: Two Newly Disclosed GeoServer Vulnerabilities Under Attack
articles.summary:
Threat actors are targeting two recently disclosed GeoServer vulnerabilities that can be chained with other flaws to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
Cybersecurity firm WatchTowr has observed attempts to exploit two high-severity GeoServer vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243. The activity appears to be aimed at identifying vulnerable servers.
“Attackers sent error-based exploit probes to validate that the server is vulnerable by creating and invoking stored queries,” WatchTowr noted.
WatchTowr has not reported any instances of attackers successfully achieving remote code execution. At the time of writing there do not appear to be any other reports of exploitation attempts.
GeoServer is an open source application for publishing and sharing geospatial data. Government agencies widely use it, and utilities also deploy it. Cybersecurity company Eye Security has identified more than 3,000 internet-accessible GeoServer instances.
CVE-2026-120705 is an XML injection vulnerability that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain sensitive files or conduct server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks. CVE-2026-129243 can enable attackers to bypass access controls and perform operations typically reserved for administrators.
The two security holes are part of a five-bug exploit chain discovered by Rapid7 researcher Jonah Burgess, aka CryptoCat, who reported his findings to GeoServer developers in early August.

articles.title: AMD's graphics chief just pushed a Radeon 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz, reportedly the fastest GPU clock ever
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: GPU overclocking records usually belong to seasoned pros who have spent years tinkering with liquid nitrogen. The newest addition to the list, however, is the man who runs AMD's computing and graphics business. Jack Huynh and a veteran overclocker pushed a Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz inside a new Micro Center in Austin. That's reportedly the highest clock speed any graphics chip has ever reached.
Huynh had come to town to celebrate the store's opening with local gamers and PC builders. On November 15, two days after the grand opening, he joined Bill "Sampson" Alverson and AMD's in-house overclocking team for a liquid-nitrogen session. He posted about it on X only this Tuesday, along with a video he says captures the exact moment the record fell.
On paper, the RX 9060 XT's boost clock tops out at 3,130 MHz, so the run pushed the chip roughly 55% past AMD's own spec. It's also nearly double the 2,530 MHz that AMD expects the card to hold in a typical game.
This is actually the third time this year that an RX 9060 XT has claimed a new high. AMD and overclocker Splave first pushed one to 4,769 MHz at the company's Markham office back in February. Then in June, Sampson and a South Korean overclocker called SoonHo edged past that with 4,789 MHz. Huynh's run tops their mark by just 48 MHz.

articles.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
articles.summary:
DoorDash has rebuilt its real-time dispatch platform to handle growing delivery demand, replacing a monolithic optimization engine with a distributed architecture that separates coordination from computation. The redesign delivers 10 times higher throughput and more than 99.99% availability during peak periods, while enabling the company to run machine learning and reinforcement learning models within dispatch workflows.
The previous dispatch engine tightly coupled business logic, logistics state management, and computationally intensive routing algorithms. As delivery volume increased, its optimization workload became increasingly difficult to process within the time available for dispatch decisions. The underlying algorithms had roughly quadratic time complexity, and during peak periods, demand approached four times the system's processing capacity. The engine consequently relied on fallback heuristics and sometimes made assignment decisions using incomplete information.
As the DoorDash engineering team explained:
The fatal bottleneck wasn't just raw machine capacity; it was the speed of reality.
Rather than address the bottleneck through conventional horizontal scaling, DoorDash redesigned the execution model around two independently scalable tiers. The engineering team described the motivation:
To scale into the future, the system didn't just need more capacity; it demanded a fundamentally new execution model.

articles.title: Diferencias entre las redes 4G y 5G: cómo funcionan y cuál es más útil para el uso diario del celular
articles.summary:
Aunque los teléfonos muestran desde hace años los símbolos 4G y 5G en la parte superior de la pantalla, muchas personas no tienen claro qué cambia entre una red y otra. La diferencia suele hacerse visible cuando una aplicación tarda en abrirse, un video se detiene o una videollamada pierde definición en un momento importante.
Las redes 4G y 5G transmiten datos a través de ondas de radio, pero ofrecen velocidades, alcance y tiempos de respuesta distintos. La elección más útil para el uso cotidiano depende de la cobertura disponible, el dispositivo y las actividades que se realizan con el celular.
Qué significa que una red sea 4G o 5G
Según Olin, la cuarta y la quinta generación de redes móviles son estándares de telecomunicaciones que permiten conectar el celular a internet sin depender de una red WiFi. La red 4G llegó al mercado en 2009 y todavía es la tecnología con mayor presencia en buena parte de las ciudades, rutas y zonas residenciales.
La red 5G comenzó su despliegue comercial en 2019. Su expansión avanza de manera gradual y requiere teléfonos compatibles, sumado a infraestructura específica de las operadoras. En la práctica, ambas permiten navegar, enviar mensajes, usar mapas, escuchar música o mirar contenidos en línea desde el celular.
Cómo funciona cada tecnología de telecomunicaciones

articles.title: Test SAV : Le SAV remplace ma TV LG OLED C1 défectueuse par une dalle neuve… déjà condamnée
articles.summary:
Pendant des années, ce qui faisait peur aux propriétaires de téléviseurs OLED, c’était le marquage (burn-in), ces images fantômes que laisse un logo affiché trop longtemps. Elles sont devenues plus rares grâce au nettoyage automatique de la dalle.
Les TV de démo, souvent éteints brutalement à la prise dans les magasins, sont les plus exposés, puisqu’en coupant le courant, on empêche le nettoyage. Mais de l’avis de mon technicien, si vous achetez un TV d’exposition et qu’il est cramé, c’est pris en charge en garantie. Un modèle d’exposition soldé peut donc être une bonne affaire, à condition de faire préciser la garantie sur la facture.
Depuis début novembre, on parle d’un autre défaut, l’edge rot qui se caractérise par des pixels morts qui apparaissent sur les bords des TV OLED à dalle LG. Mon LG OLED48C1, un 48 pouces sorti en 2021, en avait.
Mon souci, c’est que la dalle neuve que le technicien du SAV a posée ce 25 novembre a exactement les mêmes symptômes alors qu’elle était neuve, scellée et censée être en parfait état.
Première conclusion que j’en tire : quand on fait changer une dalle sous garantie, rien ne garantit que la nouvelle sera en bon état, et il vaut mieux le découvrir tant que le technicien est encore là.
J’ai repéré les premiers pixels morts il y a un mois. LG ne couvrait plus le téléviseur depuis longtemps, mais l’extension de garantie du revendeur courait toujours, et l’enseigne a accepté de le prendre en charge après un diagnostic par téléphone.

Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. A imagem mostra o fenômeno em sistema formado por dois corpos rochosos que estão sendo estudados pela agência como parte de experimento de defesa planetária.
O registro foi feito pela câmera monocromática Asteroid Framing Camera, equipamento utilizado pela espaçonave tanto para navegação quanto para observações científicas.

A diferença está nas dimensões e nas distâncias envolvidas. Dimorphos tem aproximadamente 151 metros de diâmetro e orbita Didymos a cerca de um quilômetro de distância. O asteroide maior mede aproximadamente 730 metros.
Eclipse acontece em sistema com gravidade muito baixa
Segundo Patrick Michel, principal pesquisador da missão Hera, os dois corpos estão sujeitos aos mesmos princípios da mecânica celeste que governam o sistema Terra-Lua. A diferença é que tudo acontece em escala muito menor e em ambiente de gravidade extremamente fraca.
A gravidade de Didymos é cerca de 40 mil vezes menor que a da Terra. Em Dimorphos, ela chega a ser aproximadamente 200 mil vezes mais fraca.

The company says customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.
In a security incident disclosure published today, 1Password says it began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee's GitHub account had been compromised.
The attacker used the account to access private source code repositories and inject malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records.
The stolen data includes:
- Customer names and email addresses
- Account and user IDs
- Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
- Public cryptographic keys
- Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
- Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
- Other internal account metadata
The attacker also stole internal company source code and accessed its continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.
Among the stolen customer data were tokens embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts.

articles.title: Why Y Combinator is backing fewer African startups
articles.summary:
Four years after African founders made up roughly one in 17 companies in a Y Combinator batch, the continent has become a footnote at Demo Day. The reasons say as much about how YC has changed as about African tech.
In early-2022, Y Combinator’s Winter batch included 24 African startups, 18 of them from Nigeria. For the first time, an African country ranked third in a YC cohort, behind only the United States (US) and India. Lagos founders talked about the accelerator as a rite of passage, and the Paystack exit to Stripe made the path look repeatable.
Indeed, Disrupt Africa wrote articles around that time about the “cult of Y Combinator”, and the rave reviews the programme received from founders that participated in it.
That moment did not last. By Winter 2023 the African count had fallen to three, and Winter 2024 again admitted just three. Africa’s share of a batch had shrunk from about six per cent at the peak to around one per cent by Winter 2024. A search of the YC website for African startups for the 12 batches since then returns the message “sorry, no matching companies found”.
The pullback, however, is not a single decision made in San Francisco. It is the product of three things moving at once – a YC that has changed what it wants, an African funding market that cooled faster than most, and a portfolio record that has made the case for Africa harder to argue.
The numbers: from 24, to a handful, to none

articles.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
articles.summary:
WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.
The feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.
Users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.
Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.
The feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.
WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

articles.title: BepiColombo has finally reached Mercury after an eight-year trip
articles.summary:
The big picture: BepiColombo has entered orbit around Mercury after an eight-year flight that used solar-powered electric engines and repeated planetary flybys to slow the spacecraft down. The European Space Agency said BepiColombo entered Mercury's orbit with both probes still attached. The probes will separate and take up different orbits, putting one close to the surface and sending the other much farther out to measure how Mercury's magnetic field interacts with the solar wind.
Getting to Mercury meant shedding speed, not just covering distance. After its launch in October 2018, BepiColombo had to move closer to the Sun without picking up so much speed that it overshot the planet. "Energetically, it takes more energy to go to Mercury than to go to the outer Solar System," Emma Bunce, a University of Leicester plasma physicist and one of the mission's lead scientists, told Nature.
To limit the amount of propellant it needed to carry, BepiColombo relied mainly on solar-powered electric propulsion rather than conventional thrusters. The electric propulsion system did not work entirely as planned, delaying the mission by 11 months.
The spacecraft also used gravity assists from Earth, the Moon, Venus, and Mercury over nine circuits around the Sun. Mercury itself helped slow the spacecraft before it entered orbit: BepiColombo flew past the planet six times, capturing its first close-up images of Mercury during the initial flyby in 2021.

A decade ago, digital payments in Francophone West Africa were still at an early stage, with adoption and the services available gradually expanding. Wave Mobile Money accelerated this development when it launched in the region by introducing a radically lower, flat-fee pricing structure.
The resulting price war forced established telecom-backed operators to slash their own commissions, fundamentally altering the digital payments landscape across the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). MTN MoMo eliminated withdrawal fees in Côte d’Ivoire in 2025, and Orange cut transfer fees to zero ahead of Wave’s launch in Cameroon.
For Awa Gueye, Wave’s Public Policy Lead, the true disruption is not merely in the pricing, but in the shift in consumer psychology.
“The biggest change is in what people expect,” Gueye says. “When someone sends small amounts several times a week, fees decide whether digital payments are part of daily life or reserved for emergencies. Once customers experience a low-cost, simple and reliable service, they expect that standard everywhere.”

PHP2Shell is the name for two critical PHP vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which allow unauthenticated attackers to run code remotely with the privileges of the PHP web worker.
The Fragnesia vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-46300, is a Linux kernel vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem that lets a local attacker with low-privileges to escalate permissions to root level.
An alert from CISA on October 28 warned that both security issues were being chained in attacks to deploy PHP webshells on vulnerable systems and execute commands as root.
Around the same time, Dream Security researchers reported observing a campaign using the same chain, targeting servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, including a U.S. government affiliate.
Palo Alto Networks has confirmed in an advisory today that such attacks also target firewalls running PAN-OS.
“Exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet,” reads the security bulletin.
The networking company says that all exploitation activity it observed involved PAN-OS devices that exposed their management interface to the public internet, which goes against its recommended ‘best practices.’

articles.title: How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
articles.summary:
How data centers are driving a US natural-gas boom
Rising electricity demand is locking in fossil-fuel generation.
In May 2025, my colleague David Rotman wrote a feature story describing how AI could keep us dependent on natural gas. Just 18 months later, I’ve lost count of how many times he’s already been proved right.
Sure, it’s technically possible to meet the world’s rising electricity demand with other power sources, including renewables like wind and solar supported by batteries. But the reality in the US so far is that the data center boom is helping to fuel a massive natural-gas resurgence.
Just one example: Plans for the Meta data center in Louisiana that David focused on in his story have expanded, and its power needs have too. The local utility went from three planned natural-gas plants to 10. And as I wrote in a new story this week, data center developers are now looking beyond the grid and planning to build their own off-grid gas power plants. How did we get here?
If you want to understand the future of the grid, one way to do it is by looking at interconnection queues—lists of power plants that have requested a connection to the system. In recent years these queues have been dominated by renewables like wind and solar power, which are generally the cheapest way to build new energy capacity today.

Los mensajes programados representan uno de los cambios más grandes en la historia de WhatsApp. Además, son una de las funciones más reclamadas por el público. Después de todo, la entrega automática de mensajes es una herramienta que ya lleva años disponibles en otros servicios de comunicación como plataformas de correo electrónico y de comunicación empresarial.
Usar lo nuevo de WhatsApp es realmente muy sencillo. Para dejar programado un mensaje solo tienes que crearlo y mantener pulsado sobre el botón de enviar. articles.title: User passwords safe after 1Password security breach, company says
articles.summary:
User data from 1Password has been compromised by hackers, but the company is assuring users that their passwords and recovery keys are safe.
The news: On Wednesday, 1Password announced it was subject to a breach on Nov. 19, when hackers gained access to the company’s backend system. That breach exposed the names, email addresses, and additional metadata of an unspecified number of users. Despite the attack, the Toronto-based cybersecurity software company said no passwords or recovery keys were exposed and said there is no need for users to update that information. 
From the source: “1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents,” the company wrote in a blog post on Wednesday. “Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.”
The context: 1Password uses a “vault system” that creates an encrypted container where users can control access to sensitive information like login details, credit card credentials, passkeys, and other documents. The company itself does not have access to the contents of user vaults, protecting them through dual-key encryption; access requires an account password and secret key that is not sent to or stored by 1Password servers.
1Password said the breach happened after an employee’s GitHub account was compromised and used by the attacker to introduce malware to the company’s source code. Aside from names and email addres…

articles.title: Mayo Clinic to pay workers $906,000 for unpaid time spent booting up PCs and logging in
articles.summary:
Cutting corners: Before anyone at a call center can take a call, they have to boot up their computer and log into every app the job needs. Mayo Clinic's appointment staff say they did it all off the clock. Now, the hospital system has agreed to pay them over $906,000 in back wages. The deal also gives them five paid minutes at the start of each day to get their machines running.
According to a court filing from Minnesota's attorney general, staff weren't paid for the minutes spent starting their computers and signing into the software they needed. That happened at the start of each shift and then again whenever they came back from a meal break. Mayo also rounded their clock times to the nearest 15 minutes. In the state's view, that cost them even more pay.
Mayo, for its part, doesn't agree with the state's take. But it still settled because it would rather see the money go to staff than spend it fighting the case. It had actually dropped rounding and started paying for that startup time back in May. The settlement now locks in those changes. If the clinic slips back, it could owe a $100,000 penalty.
As for the back pay, it covers 1,021 workers and every shift they put in between July 2024 and May 2026. Each worker gets 5.41 minutes of pay per shift at their individual hourly rate. Oddly enough, 4.41 of those minutes make up for the rounding alone. The total works out to an average of just under $890 per person before taxes.
The case itself started in 2025, when workers took t…

Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
Samsung is reportedly planning to increase its NAND production capacity in China, but it's unfortunately not the kind of NAND flash that will benefit regular consumers directly. As for the exact plans, the report says that Samsung will build an electroplating line in X2's empty cleanroom space, move equipment in around February 2027, and finish the conversion by November 2027. Additionally, 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line will also be switched to V9. Overall, this looks like a plan to mostly shift to denser NAND inside an existing fab, rather than a brand-new factory expansion. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so this might be more of a reshuffle. Still, the numbers suggest that a lot more NAND flash will indeed be produced according to the new plans. It looks like Samsung is doubling down on denser NAND, while TrendForce expect…

articles.summary:
Amini, a startup building sovereign AI infrastructure for governments in the Global South, has released Soma-1X Lite, an open-weight AI model designed to convert paper-based records into machine-readable data, targeting African countries that hold most public records in physical archives.
The company says the two-billion-parameter model can process about 15,000 pages per hour at an estimated graphics processing unit (GPU) computing cost of $0.22 per 1,000 pages. Dinero para armas. El precedente de Binance. articles.title: Trump doesn’t want US data centres built in Canada
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump seems to be unhappy that US hyperscalers want to build in Canada.
On Friday, Trump threatened to put “a tremendous tax” on US companies that build data centres outside of their home country. It’s not yet clear how serious the proposal was, or how he’d enforce it.
Trump’s threat could throw a wrench in Alberta’s plan to attract $100 billion in AI data-centre buildout, as well as the broader efforts to expand compute capacity across Canada. The largest developers are in the US; companies like Anthropic, Meta, and Microsoft have huge, multi-billion-dollar Canadian projects in the works. Many more have signed on to Canada’s responsible data centre development framework, signalling some intention to build in the country.
A spokesperson for Alberta Premier Danielle Smith told BetaKit in a statement that the province is aware of Trump’s threat but is waiting to see what happens. The spokesperson added that Alberta will keep working with the feds and its US partners “to make sure North America leads on AI, together.”
Aperture AI CEO Jaxson Khan, also a Munk School senior fellow and former federal policy advisor, said he’d be surprised if Trump’s comment had any major impact.
“I think this will blow over eventually after some further advocacy from the big tech giants themselves to the Trump administration,” Khan said.
Khan also pointed out that Trump just lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, where many data centre projects were also voted down. …

articles.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
articles.summary:
What happens to your private conversations when an AI company goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.
Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of users.
The attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements said.
Character.ai, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October, previously told consumers that their personal information would not be sold, the statements also noted. (In a blog post, Character.ai assured its users that their information would still be protected under its privacy policy.)
Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s plans are for the chats.

articles.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
articles.summary:
About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics.
LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online.
The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI.
They asked other physicists for some of their private gems—minor but real findings they’d never gotten around to cleaning up for public display. They were asking for real work, problems that take humans at the top of the field about a day to solve.
“Our contributors had to either sacrifice potential publication elsewhere, or else undertake a small research project just for us,” Raju wrote.
By the time all the questions and answers were ready, the AIs were, too. At a colloquium in September, Raju shared preliminary results showing that leading A…

Est-on en train d'atteindre un nouveau stade dangereux du développement des modèles IA ? C'est ce que l'on pense dorénavant beaucoup au sein des effectifs d'OpenAI et Anthropic.
Si le marché commence à avoir des doutes sur la rentabilité financière des acteurs de l'IA, avec un cours d'Anthropic déjà en train de tomber, au niveau technologique, rien n'arrête les avancées. D'après ce dernier, les start-ups américaines du secteur disposent, en interne, de modèles IA bien plus puissants que ceux qui ont été déployés. Nvidia's board accepted Huang's resignation after raising concerns about his conduct and candor, then reinstated him on Monday. articles.title: Accuracy and Resolution for Magnetic Angle Sensors
articles.summary:
Introduction
Magnetic position sensors, especially magnetic angle sensors, are the fundamental building blocks of countless motion-control applications that necessitate precision positioning. These sensors are pivotal in a wide range of industries, from automotive and robotics to consumer electronics and medical devices, underscoring their universal appeal and importance (see Figure 1).
However, to realize their full potential and utility, one must delve into two crucial parameters that govern their performance: accuracy and resolution. Although these terms are often used interchangeably, they represent distinct — albeit related — concepts in any measuring system. This comprehensive article aims to shed light on these parameters, explain how they impact the performance of magnetic position sensors, and provide guidance on optimizing these factors.
Understanding Accuracy and Resolution
Within the context of measurement and instrumentation, accuracy refers to the closeness of a measured value to the actual or true value of the quantity being measured. For magnetic position sensors, accuracy is the measure of how precisely the sensor’s angle measurement reports the actual angle. Accuracy is a way of understanding how closely the sensor’s read position corresponds to the actual position, with a high accuracy sensor producing readings that are very close to the true position.

articles.title: Clint Eastwood (96 años) hablaba así de Estados Unidos: “No hay muchas formas de arte estadounidenses que sean originales”
articles.summary:
Clint Eastwood se hizo famoso en todo el mundo como pistolero en las películas de Sergio Leone. Cuando hablaba de este género, lo hacía desde su propio punto de vista, ya que también era director. “No hay muchas formas de arte estadounidenses que sean originales”, aseguraba en un pasaje de una recopilación de sus entrevistas (publicadas entre 1968 y 1995).
“Me siento muy cercano al wéstern”. Para Eastwood, la mayor parte de las formas de arte americanas son derivadas de las tradiciones europeas. Pero hay algunas excepciones, como el cine del Oeste, el jazz o el blues. En 1987, durante el rodaje de Bird (su biopic sobre Charlie Parker), también mencionó el jazz y el wéstern como las dos aportaciones originales americanas.
Para Eastwood, el wéstern formaba parte del patrimonio cultural de Estados Unidos. El género llevó al cine las historias de frontera. Contribuyó a crear la imagen popular del Viejo Oeste.
Eastwood también dirigió y protagonizó sus propios wésterns en numerosas ocasiones. Es el caso de Infierno de cobardes (1973) o El fuera de la ley (1976). Regresó al Oeste en El jinete pálido (1985), una de sus películas favoritas, o en Sin perdón (1992, por la que recibió el Óscar a la mejor dirección en 1993). Décadas más tarde utilizó algunos elementos de este género en Cry Macho (2021).

articles.title: Voyager 1 ist einen Lichttag entfernt, sendet aber keine Daten mehr: Wie die Nasa das Problem lösen will

Ein Lichttag entfernt, aber keine Daten mehr: Nasa untersucht Panne bei Voyager 1
Am 18. November 2026 hatte Voyager 1 einen historischen Meilenstein erreicht. Als erstes menschengemachtes Objekt ist die Sonde einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt. Dies entspricht etwa 25,9 Milliarden Kilometern.
Antenne der Nasa empfing nur leeres Signal von Voyager 1
Doch kurz bevor Voyager 1 diese Marke erreicht hatte, gab es ein Problem. Die 1977 gestartete Sonde schickte keine wissenschaftlichen oder technischen Daten mehr an die Erde.
Eine Antenne des Deep Space Network der Nasa bei der australischen Hauptstadt Canberra empfing nur ein Trägersignal ohne Inhalt. Dieses Signal bestätigte immerhin, dass die Voyager die Rekordentfernung von einem Lichttag erreicht hat.
Nasa hat Bordcomputer in Verdacht
Ingenieur:innen der Nasa untersuchen laut einer Mitteilung der US-Raumfahrtbehörde, was zu der Panne geführt haben könnte. Da das Trägersignal funktioniert, liegt der Ausfall wohl nicht an der Antenne oder der Sendetechnik von Voyager 1.
Die Nasa vermutet vielmehr, dass ein Bordcomputer ausgefallen ist, der Daten der Messinstrumente der Sonde erfasst. Der Rechner wandelt diese Informationen zudem in ein richtiges Format um, damit sie zur Erde übertragen werden können.
Vor drei Jahren hatte Voyager 1 dasselbe Problem

The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.”
But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.
Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida.
The DOJ said the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers.
